decision_reason: Retain V1: elapsed first-to-last observed packet time per bidirectional flow record; UNSW seconds and CICIDS microseconds. Singleton duration is zero. Flow timeout/report boundaries remain extractor-dependent; equivalence is of the measured record quantity, not identical flow populations.

Retain V1: directional observed-packet count per bidirectional flow record, including observed retransmitted packets rather than unique sequence bytes. Direction uses the predeclared source=forward and destination=backward convention; flow boundary policies may differ. A singleton contributes one packet in its direction, zero in the other.

Reject: CICFlowMeter directional byte totals and means use transport payload lengths; Argus packet byte counters use input packet length and mean size divides those bytes by packet count. Header accounting differs and cannot be fixed by a constant unit conversion. Payload-free singleton/control packets can be zero in CICIDS but have positive full-packet size. Observed retransmission payload is accumulated again in CICFlowMeter; the historical UNSW build/config is unavailable. Same nominal direction and record aggregation do not resolve computation mismatch.

Reject as unverified: CICFlowMeter averages consecutive observed same-direction timestamp gaps (microseconds) and exports zero for <=1 packet in that direction; addPacket has no TCP-sequence deduplication. Argus combines active/idle interval means weighted by their sample counts, reports milliseconds, and defaults to zero without interval statistics. Exact UNSW interval population, historical jitter settings, retransmission/out-of-order handling and flow reporting configuration are not established. Unit conversion alone cannot establish equality.
